scope: Direct M512 first-token prefill comparison and kernel/source attribution for hipEngine, same-revision llama.cpp HIP, and same-revision llama.cpp Vulkan on one Radeon Pro W7900

matched_axes: same model file and 512 token IDs
same direct 512-row prompt batch and 512-row microbatch
BF16 K/V for the primary hipEngine versus llama.cpp HIP comparison
backend-owned synchronized prompt timing through one last-row projection
unavoidable_differences: Cross-engine reduction, activation-storage, and quant arithmetic are not bit-identical; llama.cpp HIP uses F32 graph activations and Q8_1 MMQ while hipEngine production preserves BF16 boundaries and exact F32 accumulation.
The primary Vulkan row uses native F16 K/V because RADV reports no BF16 support; a BF16-requested secondary row is included.
Top-1 equality on this stream is a protocol check, not a cross-engine logits or full quality proof.
llama.cpp server-native prompt timing splits the graph differently, so direct llama-bench M512 is primary and server-native timing is secondary.

Warmups are excluded but not shape-identical: hipEngine runs one M128 warmup and llama-bench runs its default M512 warmup. All five measured samples are reported and stable; the llama.cpp profiler child uses one explicitly no-warmup pass, while the hipEngine trace summary segments away its M128 warmup and reports the one M512 pass.

measurement_patch.effect: sets n_ctx=4096 under an environment gate, injects the fixed token IDs, and prints last-row top-1 after the timed decode

source_and_build.source_verification: Every audited file is byte-identical to git show c0bc8591e:<path>; the measurement patch applies to that revision and touches tools/llama-bench only.

secondary_native_server.interpretation: The server route is a conservative natural serving boundary; its graph splits prompt work differently and is not the primary direct-M512 comparator.

synthetic_llama_bench_context.interpretation: Replacing random pp512 IDs with the natural fixed stream changes HIP by only a few percent and does not explain the 4.10x matched gap.

comparison.finding: llama.cpp launches 1.91x as many kernels yet executes 4.16x less summed kernel time; launch count and Python submission are not the primary gap.

gap_attribution.method: Charge llama.cpp Q5 MMQ, all rocBLAS GEMM, all Q8_1 quantization, Q6 dequantization, and the residual Q4/Q6/Q8 matrix-vector kernels to this family; this intentionally overstates the llama.cpp side.
gap_attribution.why_llamacpp_is_faster: Q5_K uses a 256-thread 128-output x 128-row K256 Q8_1/WMMA MMQ tile; Q6_K at M512 dequantizes to F16 and uses rocBLAS. hipEngine's exact coltile is only four outputs x eight rows and still performs decoded-weight FP32 FMA for every output.
gap_attribution.portable_lesson: Adopt tiled activation/weight reuse, format-specific activation sum metadata, and tensorized arithmetic as explicit registered candidates; do not copy Q8_1 semantics into production without the complete quality lane.

gap_attribution.why_llamacpp_is_faster: llama.cpp processes 128 query rows and eight GQA heads per F16 WMMA FlashAttention tile, uses stream-K work partitioning, and emits 48 main plus 48 fixup dispatches. hipEngine emits 48 global plus 144 SWA exact kernels over four M128 slices and retains scalar/two-pass reference association.
gap_attribution.portable_lesson: Transfer full-M512 query tiling, head grouping, and stream-K/fixup ownership behind KVLiveSpans; begin exact-first and require the complete quality lane for any reassociated or F16/WMMA route.

gap_attribution.why_llamacpp_is_faster: llama.cpp compacts expert rows on device, Q8_1-packs each compact activation row, and applies the same 128x128/K256 MMQ framework to IQ3_XXS/IQ4_XS. hipEngine already reuses exact decoded weights across rowbatch8 but still expands the codebook and executes BF16-to-F32 FMAs.
gap_attribution.portable_lesson: Keep hipEngine's existing compact metadata, add an isolated source-faithful IQ3/IQ4 tensorized comparator, and quality-gate it independently before any stack composition.

gap_attribution.why_llamacpp_is_faster: Both engines already compact and reuse routed rows. llama.cpp Q8_1/MMQ is only 1.14x faster than hipEngine's exact pair16 grouped body, so changed arithmetic has little remaining reward here.
gap_attribution.portable_lesson: Defer IQ2. The prior P6 quality and sparse-repair failures remain authoritative.

source_findings: MMVQ_MAX_BATCH_SIZE is 8; M512 enters MMQ. RDNA3 high-expert MUL_MAT_ID selects MMQ unconditionally for this 256-expert model.

The RDNA WMMA config offers 256-thread, I=128, J up to 128, K=256 tiles for Q5_K, Q6_K, IQ2_XS, IQ3_XXS, and IQ4_XS; the trace selects J=128 and reports VGPR232-248 with zero scratch for the dominant MMQs.
quantize_mmq_q8_1 uses one scale per 32 values for these formats, packs four int8 values per store, and records format-specific partial sums where affine min terms need them.

For broadcast gate/up inputs, mm_ids_helper builds the inverse compact mapping and quantize_scatter_mmq_q8_1 quantizes one physical token row before writing its top-k compact slots. hipEngine already owns equivalent compact metadata, so the helper itself should not be ported.

At M512 dense Q5_K selects custom MMQ, while dense Q6_K exceeds gfx1100's <=128 MMQ cutoff and falls through to dequantization plus rocBLAS; a blanket claim that all llama.cpp dense projections use MMQ is incorrect.

The traced FlashAttention body is flash_attn_ext_f16<128,128,8,8> plus one general stream-K fixup per layer. Dynamic shared tiling and F16 WMMA, not merely two fewer launches per layer, explain the 22.6x attention-family delta.

ranked_next_lanes.name: dense Q5/Q6 tensorized tile
ranked_next_lanes.exact_first: Screen larger distributed output-row tiles that preserve each output's K ownership and reduction tree, with source bytes and activations staged once per K tile.
ranked_next_lanes.changed_arithmetic_fallback: Only after the exact tile ceiling is measured, compare the existing rejected D4/D8/D8R8 surfaces with a source-faithful F32-to-Q8_1 128x128/K256 MMQ leaf. A new result must be materially different from those rejected variants and pass the full 18-prompt/576-step gate.

ranked_next_lanes.name: full-M512 tiled FlashAttention
ranked_next_lanes.exact_first: Extend adjacent-query K/V reuse beyond qrow4 while preserving KVLiveSpans and exact per-row reduction order; remove the four-M128 attention slicing where safe.
ranked_next_lanes.changed_arithmetic_fallback: Isolate a compensated F16/WMMA 128-query, multi-head, stream-K route with an unfused exact fallback and the complete quality lane; the rejected online qrow4 route cannot be treated as reusable quality evidence.

ranked_next_lanes.name: IQ3/IQ4 selected-down tensorized tile
ranked_next_lanes.exact_first: Reprice larger exact expert-major row/output tiles and one-time codebook expansion without changing the existing compact metadata ABI.
ranked_next_lanes.changed_arithmetic_fallback: Add a standalone source-faithful Q8_1 IQ3/IQ4 MMQ comparator and run quality independently before composing with any dense or attention approximation.

ranked_next_lanes.name: IQ2 residual and launch tail
ranked_next_lanes.action: Defer until H1-H3 are measured; do not reopen P6 or WPF-4 while IQ2 is only a 56.97-ms gap and span-minus-sum is 15.21 ms.

campaign_revision.long_context_policy: Keep 16K+ closed. First reach matched direct M512 >=694.184 tok/s, then collect a matched llama.cpp HIP M4K comparator before reopening long-context work; retain 800/700 tok/s at M512/M4K as stretch targets rather than the only evidence of attainable hardware performance.
campaign_revision.no_gaming: Every changed-arithmetic lane uses the complete train+heldout prompt/category gate and category heldouts; the fixed M512 stream is attribution only and cannot promote a candidate.
